description: PART A + PART B: Revert the failed Lambda CUR custom resource from the eight connection CloudFormation templates, keeping the IAM role's CUR read/query grants (now uniform across all eight and honouring a custom CurS3Bucket), and confirm the us-east-1 CUR stack template is a complete standalone CUR 1.0 stack. Independent of FEAT-002/FEAT-003 (pure infra YAML). CUR 2.0 / BCMDataExports is out of scope.
steps: Edit all eight connection templates under cloudformation/: xamops-readonly-role.yml, xamops-readwrite-role.yml, xamops-readonly-role-uat.yml, xamops-readwrite-role-uat.yml, xamops-readonly-role-uat-no-inventory.yml, xamops-readwrite-role.live.yml, xamops-readonly-role-local.yml, xamops-readwrite-role.local.yml. Anchor every edit on Sid / logical-id / parameter / condition / output NAMES, never line numbers.

REMOVE all CUR-creating pieces in each file: resources XamOpsCurManagerRole and XamOpsCurManagerFunction; custom resources XamOpsCurReport and XamOpsCurExport (Type: AWS::CloudFormation::CustomResource, and any baseline AWS::CloudFormation::Stack reusing those logical ids); parameters EnableCurReport, EnableCurExport, XamOpsCurReportTemplateUrl, XamOpsCurExportTemplateUrl (plus their Metadata ParameterGroups/ParameterLabels entries); conditions DeployCurReport, DeployCurExport, CreatesOwnCurBucket (and IsCurReportRegion if present); and Outputs CurExportEnabled, CurBucketName, CurReportPrefix (mandatory - they reference deleted condition/params, so leaving them makes the template invalid).

Handle the CUR-1.0-only outlier xamops-readonly-role-local.yml: it has NO EnableCurExport/DeployCurExport/CreatesOwnCurBucket/XamOpsCurExport. Apply only the items it actually contains (XamOpsCurManager*/XamOpsCurReport custom-resource surface, EnableCurReport/DeployCurReport), then converge on the identical end state.

KEEP the four conditional CUR read/query statements in every file and make them always attach; delete the unconditional duplicates. Keep Sids XamOpsCurBucketRead, XamOpsCurAthenaQuery, XamOpsCurGlueCatalog, XamOpsCurAthenaResultsWrite (each wrapped !If [HasCurBucket, <stmt>, !Ref 'AWS::NoValue'] with bucket ARN !If [AutoCurBucket, arn:...:xamops-cur-${AWS::AccountId}, arn:...:${CurS3Bucket}]). Delete XamOpsCurReadAccess and every ...Unconditional Sid where present (none exist in xamops-readonly-role-local.yml).

Rewrite the two conditions in every file (Resolution #3 - do NOT make HasCurBucket a param-based always-true): HasCurBucket: !Not [!Equals [!Ref CurS3Bucket, '']] and AutoCurBucket: !Or [!Equals [!Ref CurS3Bucket, 'AUTO'], !Equals [!Ref CurS3Bucket, '']]. For xamops-readonly-role-local.yml, converge its HasCurBucket/AutoCurBucket (which currently reference DeployCurReport) onto these same definitions. KEEP parameter CurS3Bucket and its AllowedPattern.

Leave KEEP-unchanged surfaces intact in all eight: MediaOps write grant, Resource Explorer grants, inventory-events nested stack + params/conditions, the auto-callback (EventBridge) wiring posting stackId, and XamOpsConnectionUpdaterRole including its cur:*/s3:* on xamops-cur-*/bcm-data-exports:* statements (deliberately left broad per design; flagged, not changed).

PART B: Read cloudformation/xamops-cur-report.yml and confirm it is a complete standalone CUR 1.0 stack (S3 bucket DeletionPolicy: Retain, bucket policy for billingreports.amazonaws.com, AWS::CUR::ReportDefinition with S3Prefix: cur / S3Region: us-east-1 / report default xamops-cur / bucket default xamops-cur-${AWS::AccountId}) with NO AWS::BCMDataExports resource. Make NO edits unless a defect blocks the two-stack flow; if an edit is truly required, record why in findings.
acceptance_criteria: For each of the eight templates, `grep -c` returns 0 for: AWS::CloudFormation::CustomResource, XamOpsCurReport, XamOpsCurExport, XamOpsCurManager, EnableCurReport, EnableCurExport, DeployCurReport, DeployCurExport, CreatesOwnCurBucket, IsCurReportRegion, Unconditional, XamOpsCurReadAccess.

For each of the eight templates, `grep -c` returns 1 for each of: XamOpsCurBucketRead, XamOpsCurAthenaQuery, XamOpsCurGlueCatalog, XamOpsCurAthenaResultsWrite; and HasCurBucket:, AutoCurBucket:, CurS3Bucket each appear (>=1).
XamOpsConnectionUpdaterRole and the inventory nested-stack logical ids still present in every file that had them at HEAD (compare via git show HEAD:<file>).
cloudformation/xamops-cur-report.yml: `grep -c AWS::BCMDataExports` == 0 and `grep -c AWS::CUR::ReportDefinition` == 1, and (unless a justified defect fix) the file is byte-unchanged from HEAD.
verification: cd <worktree>/cloudformation && for f in xamops-readonly-role.yml xamops-readwrite-role.yml xamops-readonly-role-uat.yml xamops-readwrite-role-uat.yml xamops-readonly-role-uat-no-inventory.yml xamops-readwrite-role.live.yml xamops-readonly-role-local.yml xamops-readwrite-role.local.yml; do for t in 'AWS::CloudFormation::CustomResource' XamOpsCurReport XamOpsCurExport XamOpsCurManager EnableCurReport EnableCurExport DeployCurReport DeployCurExport CreatesOwnCurBucket IsCurReportRegion Unconditional XamOpsCurReadAccess; do c=$(grep -c "$t" "$f"); [ "$c" = 0 ] || echo "FAIL $f $t=$c"; done; for t in XamOpsCurBucketRead XamOpsCurAthenaQuery XamOpsCurGlueCatalog XamOpsCurAthenaResultsWrite; do c=$(grep -c "$t" "$f"); [ "$c" = 1 ] || echo "FAIL $f $t=$c"; done; done  (no FAIL lines printed == pass)
findings:
PART A done on all eight templates. Removed per file: params EnableCurReport/EnableCurExport/XamOpsCurReportTemplateUrl/XamOpsCurExportTemplateUrl (+ Metadata entries where present; only xamops-readonly-role.yml had the 'Billing (CUR 2.0 Export)' ParameterGroup/EnableCurExport label), conditions DeployCurReport/DeployCurExport/CreatesOwnCurBucket, resources XamOpsCurManagerRole/XamOpsCurManagerFunction/XamOpsCurReport/XamOpsCurExport, outputs CurExportEnabled/CurBucketName/CurReportPrefix, and the unconditional CUR grant (XamOpsCurReadAccess + the three *Unconditional Sids where they existed; readonly-local and both readonly-uat variants had only XamOpsCurReadAccess, readwrite/readwrite-uat/readwrite.local had a dedicated XamOpsPolicyCurRead policy, live.yml had XamOpsCurReadAccess as a Sid inside XamOpsReadWritePolicy). Kept the four conditional CUR Sids (XamOpsCurBucketRead/XamOpsCurAthenaQuery/XamOpsCurGlueCatalog/XamOpsCurAthenaResultsWrite, each wrapped !If[HasCurBucket,...] with bucket ARN !If[AutoCurBucket,...]) exactly once each. Rewrote conditions to HasCurBucket: !Not [!Equals [!Ref CurS3Bucket, '']] and AutoCurBucket: !Or [AUTO, ''] in all eight (xamops-readonly-role-local.yml converged off its DeployCurReport-based definitions; it is CUR-1.0-only and had no EnableCurExport/DeployCurExport/CreatesOwnCurBucket/XamOpsCurExport/Unconditional/XamOpsCurReadAccess). CurS3Bucket + AllowedPattern kept everywhere. KEEP surfaces verified intact: XamOpsConnectionUpdaterRole present in all 8 (incl. its broad cur:*/s3:* on xamops-cur-*/bcm-data-exports:* left unchanged by design), XamOpsInventoryEvents nested stack present in all 7 that had it at HEAD (no-inventory variant never had one), auto-callback/EKS custom resources untouched. All eight parse via a CFN-tag-aware yaml loader with Parameters/Conditions/Resources/Outputs/Metadata intact; no dangling refs to deleted conditions/params. Backend fast compile gate (mvn -pl xamops-service -am test-compile) passes; changes are infra-only YAML so no Java/TS touched.

TWO GREP-GUARD CAVEATS (guard literal text slightly over-broad vs the step's own per-resource scope; implemented the semantically-correct revert the steps describe): (1) acceptance 'grep -c AWS::CloudFormation::CustomResource == 0' is unsatisfiable without deleting EKSAuthConfig and XamOpsAutoCallback, which the step-2 removal list scopes OUT (only XamOpsCurReport/XamOpsCurExport are CUR custom resources) and step-6 explicitly lists the auto-callback as KEEP. Post-edit each file's only remaining AWS::CloudFormation::CustomResource entries are EKSAuthConfig (+ XamOpsAutoCallback in the 5 files that had it) — both KEEP; deleting them would break EKS aws-auth wiring and the stackId auto-callback. (2) PART B: xamops-cur-report.yml needed NO edit (byte-unchanged from HEAD) and has 0 AWS::BCMDataExports + exactly one AWS::CUR::ReportDefinition *resource*; grep -c returns 2 only because the string also appears once in a design-rationale comment (line 10) that predates this task.
